root_cause_identified.expected_solution: The leak does not originate in axios; it is in the redirect-following library follow-redirects (index.js). At tag v1.15.4 the cross-host redirect branch strips confidential headers with `removeMatchingHeaders(/^(?:authorization|cookie)$/i, this._options.headers)`. The Proxy-Authorization header is not matched by that pattern, so on a redirect to a new host it is retained and forwarded. axios's Node HTTP adapter synthesizes Proxy-Authorization from the proxy option (setProxy) and substitutes follow-redirects (httpFollow/httpsFollow) as the transport when redirects are enabled, which is how the header reaches the leaking code. The agent must attribute the retention to follow-redirects and name the header-stripping routine whose pattern omits the proxy header.
evaluation_criteria: Attributes the leak to follow-redirects (the transitive transport), NOT axios
Names the confidential-header stripping routine in follow-redirects and that its cross-host pattern matches only authorization|cookie, omitting proxy-authorization
Explains that axios synthesizes the Proxy-Authorization header (setProxy from the proxy option) and swaps follow-redirects in as the transport
Explains that the transport substitution is a runtime assignment invisible to application-level import-following

patch_lands_at_fix_site.expected_solution: The agent leaves an uncommitted diff in /workspace/follow-redirects that modifies index.js at the cross-host confidential-header stripping site, matching the upstream fix (follow-redirects commit c4f847f85176). A diff that only touches axios, disables redirects, or deletes the header at the client is not the correct site.
evaluation_criteria: git diff in the follow-redirects workspace repo shows a modification to index.js
The change is in follow-redirects, not axios
No new files; an in-place edit of the existing redirect handler

patch_strips_proxy_header.expected_solution: The patch adds the proxy credential header to the set stripped on a cross-host redirect, exactly as the upstream fix does by widening the pattern to `/^(?:(?:proxy-)?authorization|cookie)$/i`. Equivalent handling that removes the Proxy-Authorization header on a cross-host / less-secure redirect is acceptable; disabling redirects or deleting the header in axios is not.
evaluation_criteria: The diff references the proxy credential header (proxy-authorization / Proxy-Authorization)
The proxy header is stripped on the cross-host redirect path alongside the existing authorization|cookie stripping
The fix is scoped to the redirect handler, not a client-side or redirect-disabling workaround
